articles.title: Accesso Adds 100+ AI Decision Skills to Its Attractions Intelligence Platform
articles.summary: Accesso has expanded its AI-powered accesso Intelligence platform with a library of over 100 pre-built Decision Skills, drawing on 25 years of industry experience and a decade of data expertise from its Dexibit acquisition. The tool gives attraction operators reusable AI-driven approaches to everyday operational decisions without requiring staff to become prompt engineers. For FEC operators, this lowers the barrier to adopting AI for tasks like staffing, pricing, and guest flow management.

articles.title: Accesso Intelligence Launches 100+ Decision Skills for Visitor Attractions
articles.summary: Accesso Technology Group has officially announced the rollout of more than 100 Decision Skills within its accesso Intelligence AI platform, aimed at helping attraction operators make faster, more consistent decisions. The library packages decades of sector-specific knowledge into reusable AI workflows covering operations, revenue, and guest experience. FEC operators exploring AI adoption will find this a practical entry point with low technical overhead.

articles.title: Connect&GO: Four Ways Operators Can Reduce Guest Journey Friction
articles.summary: Connect&GO, drawing on conversations at IAAPA Expo Europe 2026, outlines four strategies for creating a seamless connected guest journey across admissions, F&B, retail, and rides using integrated RFID and technology solutions. The core insight is that guests experience an entire day out as one event and feel every friction point across departmental handoffs. For FEC operators, the message is clear: integrated systems are no longer a luxury but a baseline guest expectation.

articles.title: Cinchio and Vantage Integrate RFID Wristbands with Self-Service F&B Kiosks
articles.summary: Cinchio and WhiteWater's Vantage platform have partnered to allow guests to use RFID wristbands at self-service food and beverage kiosks, streamlining checkout and reducing queue bottlenecks at amusement parks, water parks, and other attractions. The integration connects self-service ordering directly to kitchen workflows and operational dashboards, giving operators better visibility and throughput. FEC operators with cashless wristband systems should take note of this as a model for reducing F&B friction.

articles.title: Gateway Ticketing on How AI Agents Could Reshape Attraction Ticket Sales
articles.summary: Gateway Ticketing Systems is exploring how AI-powered commerce agents — software that researches, compares, and purchases on behalf of consumers — could become a significant new distribution channel for attractions. Operators may need to restructure their inventory data and availability feeds to remain visible and bookable in an AI-mediated search environment. FEC operators who rely on online ticketing should begin thinking about how their data architecture will perform in an agentic commerce world.

articles.title: How Dream Garden Builds FECs Tailored to Different Markets
articles.summary: InPark Magazine profiles Dream Garden, an FEC development company that takes a customized concept-to-opening approach depending on target market demographics and geography. The article examines how the company adapts attraction mix, design, and operational models to suit distinct communities. This is directly relevant for FEC developers and investors evaluating new builds or rebrands.

articles.title: New Idaho FEC Extreme Rush Closes Just Six Months After Opening
articles.summary: Extreme Rush, an indoor entertainment center in Pocatello, Idaho, appears to have shuttered only six months after its grand opening, raising questions about its viability. The closure left customers holding unused gift cards, prompting two local businesses to step in and honor them. The situation serves as a cautionary tale for FEC operators about the importance of market analysis, capitalization, and customer trust in early operations.

articles.title: Local Businesses Honor Unused Gift Cards After Idaho FEC Shuts Down
articles.summary: Following the closure of Extreme Rush in Pocatello, Idaho, two neighboring businesses stepped up to redeem unused gift cards for affected customers, generating significant goodwill. The story highlights both the reputational risks FECs face when closing abruptly and the community relations opportunities for businesses that respond generously. FEC operators should consider gift card liability management as part of their financial planning.

articles.title: Launch Entertainment Opens New Indoor FEC in Pensacola, Florida
articles.summary: Launch Entertainment has debuted a new indoor family entertainment center in Pensacola, Florida, continuing the brand's multi-unit expansion across the U.S. The venue adds to a growing wave of large-format indoor FECs entering secondary markets. Operators and investors tracking FEC chain growth will want to monitor Launch's footprint expansion strategy.

articles.title: Massive Launch Entertainment Center Opens in Pensacola
articles.summary: A large new entertainment center called Massive Launch has opened in Pensacola, Florida, bringing a multi-attraction indoor FEC experience to the Gulf Coast market. The opening reflects continued investor and operator confidence in secondary-market FEC locations in the Southeast. Local operators in the region should be aware of the new competitive presence.

articles.title: The Game Palacio Opens Its 14th Entertainment Centre
articles.summary: The Game Palacio has expanded to a 14th location, signaling robust growth for the multi-unit entertainment center brand. Multi-location FEC chains are increasingly demonstrating the scalability of the format across different markets. This is a useful benchmark for operators and investors evaluating branded FEC growth models.

articles.title: Imagicaaworld Sells Hotel, Acquires Water Park Stake, Targets Indoor Entertainment Expansion
articles.summary: India-based Imagicaaworld is restructuring its asset portfolio by selling its hotel property and acquiring a stake in a water park while signaling a strategic push into indoor entertainment. The move reflects a broader global trend of entertainment companies consolidating around core experiential assets and FEC-style indoor venues. Investors tracking international FEC market development should follow Imagicaaworld's pivot closely.

articles.title: Indian FEC Developer Complete Sports and Management Wins Two New Projects
articles.summary: Complete Sports and Management India (BSE: CSML) has secured contracts for two new FEC projects, reflecting growing demand for family entertainment infrastructure in the Indian market. The wins signal continued investment in the FEC sector in South Asia, a market drawing increasing attention from global suppliers and developers. Suppliers looking to expand into emerging markets should note the momentum in India's FEC pipeline.

articles.title: Construction Underway on Two Hello Park Locations
articles.summary: Hello Park, an indoor entertainment concept, has broken ground on two new locations, advancing its multi-site expansion plan. The brand's simultaneous build-out of multiple venues reflects the growing appetite for scaled FEC development. Operators and suppliers interested in emerging FEC brands should monitor Hello Park's growth trajectory.

articles.title: Time Mission Escape Room Concept Plans 2027 Arizona Opening
articles.summary: Time Mission, an escape room entertainment concept, has announced plans to open a Scottsdale, Arizona location in 2027, expanding its footprint into the competitive Southwest U.S. market. The announcement reflects continued investor confidence in immersive, story-driven entertainment as a durable FEC category. Operators in the Phoenix metro area should factor a new premium escape room competitor into their planning.

articles.title: Gresham Wunderland Closes Theater, Plans FEC Expansion
articles.summary: Oregon's Gresham Wunderland entertainment center is shutting down its on-site movie theater and redirecting resources toward expanding its core FEC attractions. The move illustrates a broader industry pattern of FECs pruning underperforming passive entertainment elements in favor of active, participatory experiences. Operators evaluating their own attraction mix should take note of this strategic reallocation.

articles.title: Nostalgia Drives Rebirth of Wisconsin Bowling Alley
articles.summary: A bowling alley in Ozaukee County, Wisconsin is being revived, with the owner citing community nostalgia and pent-up demand as key drivers for the investment. The story reflects a broader trend of bowling venues being repositioned as community anchors with updated amenities. FEC operators considering bowling as an anchor attraction will find the business case here instructive.

articles.title: UK Snooker Hall Plans Conversion to Six-Lane Bowling and Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A snooker hall in West Cumbria, England is seeking to reinvent itself as a bowling and indoor entertainment venue, reflecting the ongoing repurposing of legacy leisure facilities into modern FEC-style attractions. The conversion trend is notable for FEC operators and real estate investors looking at underutilized leisure properties. This type of adaptive reuse is increasingly common as bowling and multi-attraction formats prove more durable than single-activity venues.

articles.title: Universal Theme Parks Revenue Falls 4% Amid Macro Headwinds and Epic Universe Comparisons
articles.summary: Comcast reported a 4.4% decline in Universal theme parks revenue and a 17.1% drop in adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026, attributing the softness to macroeconomic pressures and tough year-over-year comparisons following Epic Universe's June 2025 opening. Executives acknowledged competitors were faster to adapt marketing to softer demand conditions. For FEC operators, the results are a reminder that even major players are navigating consumer spending caution, and agile marketing responses matter.

articles.title: TEA Annual Report: Attendance at World's Top 25 Theme Parks Essentially Flat in 2025
articles.summary: The Themed Entertainment Association's Index 2025 report finds that attendance at the world's 25 leading theme parks was largely unchanged year over year, suggesting the post-pandemic surge has normalized. For FEC operators, a plateau at large theme parks may signal opportunity to capture guests seeking more accessible, value-oriented local entertainment. Tracking attendance trends at major parks helps FEC operators understand the broader competitive landscape.

articles.title: IRT Launches Quarterly Manufacturer-Operator Live Chat Series
articles.summary: Industry Round Table (IRT) is introducing a new quarterly virtual series bringing FEC manufacturers and operators together to discuss challenges, best practices, and emerging opportunities, starting with short educational presentations followed by interactive breakout discussions. The format is designed to facilitate direct dialogue between the supply and operating sides of the industry. FEC operators and suppliers should consider participating to stay current on peer insights and product developments.

articles.title: Experience UK Launches Free Readiness Benchmark for Attraction Operators
articles.summary: Experience UK has introduced a complimentary Experience Readiness Benchmark tool to help its members assess their capabilities across audience engagement, digital maturity, AI readiness, and operational performance. Participants receive a personalized report with their overall readiness score and growth priorities. While UK-focused, the diagnostic framework is broadly applicable and useful for any FEC operator looking to identify gaps before investing in new technologies or programs.

articles.title: WAVE Aquatic Safety Names New Leadership Team After ACB Safety Products Acquisition
articles.summary: WAVE Aquatic Safety, a developer of AI-powered drowning detection technology, has announced a new executive team as it enters a growth phase following its acquisition by ACB Safety Products International. The leadership transition positions WAVE for broader commercial deployment of its safety technology in aquatic facilities. FEC operators running water parks, aquatic attractions, or pool areas should monitor WAVE's expanded go-to-market push.

articles.title: 'Masha and the Three Bears' Brings Licensed LBE Concept to Middle East
articles.summary: The popular animated IP 'Masha and the Three Bears' is making its debut in location-based entertainment in the Middle East, entering a market that has shown strong appetite for IP-driven family attractions. The move is part of a broader global trend of entertainment brands expanding into LBE formats as a licensing revenue stream. FEC operators evaluating IP partnerships for their venues should watch how this rollout performs in the region.

articles.title: Why Experience Design Must Be Built Into the Master Plan, Not Added On
articles.summary: A Blooloop analysis argues that too many destination developers commission experience design late in the process, limiting its impact and making it harder to justify investment. The piece makes a case for integrating creative thinking into masterplanning and commercial strategy from the outset to create differentiated destinations that drive repeat visits. FEC developers and designers will find the strategic framework useful when pitching or planning new builds.

articles.title: Winner's Circle FEC Marks Two Years in Longmont with Regional Recognition
articles.summary: Winner's Circle in Longmont, Colorado is celebrating its two-year anniversary with regional industry recognition and customer anniversary promotions, highlighting the venue's successful establishment in its market. The milestone reflects the viability of multi-attraction FEC formats in mid-size Colorado communities. Operators in similar-sized markets can look to Winner's Circle's growth arc as a useful case study.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 112: IAAPA Expo 2026 Coverage
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's Issue 112 provides comprehensive coverage of IAAPA Expo 2026, the attractions industry's premier annual trade show, with an interactive table of contents guiding readers to key stories. IAAPA Expo content is essential reading for FEC operators tracking new products, supplier announcements, and industry trends. Operators who could not attend in person should use this issue to catch up on key developments.

articles.title: PIXERA Platform Syncs 19 Projectors for Czech Immersive Art Venue
articles.summary: The PIXERA media server platform is being used to synchronize 19 projectors across Signal Space, a nearly 27,000-square-foot digital art gallery in the Czech Republic that opened in 2025. The technical case study demonstrates the scalability of projection mapping software for large immersive entertainment environments. FEC operators developing immersive digital experiences or projection-based attractions will find the technical execution details relevant.

articles.title: Top 10 Bowling Equipment Manufacturers of 2026: What Operators Should Know
articles.summary: A roundup of the leading bowling equipment manufacturers in 2026 highlights how the industry is advancing with modern technology, updated lane systems, and enhanced entertainment integrations. For FEC operators with bowling as a core offering, the list provides a useful overview of the competitive supplier landscape. Operators planning renovations or new builds should cross-reference this list when evaluating vendors.

articles.title: Henderson Sport & Social Opens with Volleyball, Laser Tag, and Bar Concept
articles.summary: Henderson Sport & Social has opened in the Las Vegas metro area, combining recreational sports leagues, laser tag, and a bar and social concept into a single venue targeting adult demographics. The hybrid social entertainment model continues to gain traction as an alternative to traditional FEC formats. Operators exploring adult-oriented entertainment strategies should monitor how this venue performs in a highly competitive leisure market.
